Choose this for a substantial handoff

Doc Coauthoring helps transfer context, refine a structure and challenge the draft with reader questions. DOCX handles the Word deliverable. Choose this combination for a workshop retrospective, an internal proposal or an operating guide. For a short email, a normal prompt is usually enough.

This is a source-based editorial pick for structured writing, not a benchmark winner. It cannot validate missing facts or supply your organisation’s approval.

Choose your app before installing

Beginner route: use a paid Claude.ai plan with file creation and the relevant skills enabled for your account. Anthropic’s repository describes its example skills as available on paid plans. Start with the document tools enabled for your account; this route needs no terminal.

Local route: use Claude Code with file access and eligible paid or API access. The commands below install both the example collection and document collection. A plugin is a package; Doc Coauthoring and DOCX are individual skills inside those packages.

/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills

Confirm both collections in /plugin. Local Word production also needs the runtime tools the DOCX skill uses: Node’s docx package, and tools such as Pandoc, LibreOffice and Poppler for reading or rendering. The hosted environment’s preinstalled tools are not guaranteed on your computer. Ask the agent to check availability before generating; follow upstream setup rather than assuming installation succeeded.

1. Build a small source pack

Create a copy of approved notes and a short facts file. Include audience, purpose, required headings, source dates, the reporting period and unresolved questions. Use a practice example with invented data labelled as synthetic. Keep customer details and confidential attachments out of the exercise.

For a workshop retrospective, supply actual attendance, feedback you are allowed to use, observed problems and the decisions already made. Missing feedback stays unknown.

2. Agree the content before formatting

Use Doc Coauthoring to prepare a two-page workshop retrospective for an operations lead.
Read only the source files I supplied. First list confirmed facts, proposals and missing information.
Ask for the decisions needed before drafting.
Propose a structure covering outcomes, observations, actions, owners and unresolved questions.
Keep evidence dates and source references visible. Do not invent participant quotes or outcomes.
After we approve the draft, give me five questions a new reader should be able to answer.

Review the draft section by section. Then open a fresh conversation with only the draft and the five questions. Check whether the answers are supported by the document. Then check the draft with an intended reader.

3. Produce an editable Word handoff

Use DOCX to turn the approved draft into workshop-retrospective.docx.
Use semantic heading styles, page numbers, a readable action table and descriptive links.
Keep source references and unresolved questions. Preserve the original notes.
Return the editable Word file and a rendering or preview if available.
Tell me which checks actually ran and which could not run. Do not send or publish it.

Expected output: a downloadable .docx with editable content. Download and open it in your intended Word-compatible app.

4. Accept it only after these checks

  • Compare names, dates, counts and quoted statements against the source pack.
  • Use the document navigation pane to check the heading hierarchy.
  • Inspect every page for split tables, clipped text and unwanted blank pages.
  • Confirm each action has an owner or an explicit unassigned status; proposals must remain proposals.
  • Open and edit the file in the app your recipient will use.

If local rendering is unavailable, mark visual validation incomplete and inspect manually. If the file will not open, retain the approved plain-text draft and ask the agent to diagnose the export. Disable unneeded plugin collections through the plugin manager. Keep original files and a clearly named revision so you can discard the generated copy.
